sources.title: First-party/official body: https://www.varonis.com/blog/cosnitch
sources.role: Post-Screening exact authority supplement: first-party announcement/docs/changelog body inspected for capability, availability, chronology, and API/functional facts; marketing framing separated

claims.text: Varonis's Aug 18 publication describes a three-flaw chain in Copilot Personal: crafted-URL automatic prompt execution, connected-app data collection/exfiltration, and persistent memory poisoning.
claims.context: Researcher publication in captured Varonis body (265189B); no MSRC citation.

claims.text: The publication states Microsoft shipped server-side patches Aug 18, 2026, names only Copilot Personal (consumer, copilot.microsoft.com), and reports no observed in-the-wild exploitation.
claims.context: Scope/patch statements; researcher-attributed only, no vendor quotation.

claims.text: The researcher publication uses CVE-2026-24301 as the tracking ID (CVSS 8.8-class, CWE-77 as researcher-stated); MSRC bytes are uncaptured, so no vendor corroboration is claimed here.
claims.context: Researcher-attributed identifier/scope; MSRC 2717B shell is captured-but-unconsumed for advisory content and is not cited as corroboration.

limitations.text: MSRC advisory bytes are captured-but-unconsumed (2717B JS shell, no CVE bytes); vendor severity/product-scope wording is researcher-attributed, not vendor-quoted.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Exploitability details beyond the researcher's account are not independently tested in captured bytes.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

targets.target: One-click chain involved automatic prompt execution, connected-app data exfiltration and persistent-memory poisoning; Varonis says patches shipped Aug 18 and no exploitation was observed. Distinguish Copilot Personal from Microsoft 365 Copilot.
targets.finding: One-click chain (auto-execution, exfiltration, memory poisoning), Aug 18 patches, no observed exploitation, and Personal-vs-M365 scope all VERIFIED in captured Varonis researcher body (265189B). MSRC 2717B shell is captured-but-unconsumed and not cited; vendor severity/scope wording stays researcher-attributed (UNRESOLVED vendor part held in claims/limitations, overall PARTIAL).
